conventions.convention: Representation fields are measurable for each fixed group element; fibre group laws hold everywhere. Strong continuity of the integral is separately proved for second-countable locally compact Hausdorff groups.
Bases carry sigma-finite Borel measures and need not be complete. General Borel projections are completion-measurable; selectors and Borel versions are obtained on conull Borel subsets.

Factor representations have nonzero carriers. The group type-I definition tests separable factor representations; positive multiplicity is finite or countably infinite. A minimal projection in the generated algebra gives the multiplicity space, whereas one in its commutant gives an irreducible carrier.

The Mackey structure is the quotient Borel structure of irreducible representations on fixed positive finite or countably infinite carriers, using weak compact-uniform group coefficients. Countable separation is a separate property.
Monomial induction uses left cosets Ht and right multiplication tg=α(t,g)(t·g), with action π(g)f(t)=χ(α(t,g))f(t·g).
Normality of a positive functional means relative WOT continuity on the operator-norm unit ball. The discrete right regular action is ρ(g)f(h)=f(hg).

Atomicity concerns the effective canonical compact-group isotypic model; redundant parameter measures need not be atomic, and zero-carrier atoms must be discarded before applying nonzero-fibre uniqueness.
The real-line example uses positive-phase Plancherel obtained by composing the library's conjugate-phase transform with dual inversion.

Hermitian pairings are linear in the first variable. With g=ρ(dx²+dy²) and h(e,e)=ψ, the complex orientation is dx∧dy and the conjugate-linear bundle star sends u dbar z⊗e to −iψ conjugate(u) dz⊗e*. Its degree-one square is −1.

The Dolbeault operator is the maximal weak L² operator; its adjoint is the Hilbert adjoint. Laplacian domains require the indicated compositions, and harmonic kernels are initially Hilbert-domain kernels rather than spaces of smooth forms.

The Laplacian Fourier symbol is positive, ½|ξ|²_g; the scalar-polynomial principal-symbol convention gives its negative. Sobolev spaces are finite-chart completions. The form with an added L² term represents I+Δ'', not Δ''.

Dolbeault cohomology uses smooth forms. Its duality pairing is complex-bilinear integration of u∧α; the star identification is conjugate-linear. Full AC is retained by the analytic results; the metric-definition interfaces use Countable Choice.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. For a second-countable locally compact group, the type-I condition, standardness of the Mackey dual together with equality of Mackey and Fell Borel structures, countable separation, and the primitive-kernel homeomorphism condition are equivalent.

Assume AC. A measurable field of unital von Neumann algebras on separable measurable Hilbert fibres over a sigma-finite standard-Borel measured base has measurable commutant and centre fields, a von Neumann direct integral, fibrewise commutant and centre identities, and almost-everywhere uniqueness of fields with equal direct integrals.

Assume AC. Every strongly continuous unitary representation of a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff group on a nonzero separable Hilbert space has a sigma-finite standard-Borel central decomposition with almost-everywhere nonzero factor fibres, diagonal centre, and fibrewise generated-algebra and commutant identities.

Assume AC. A separable strongly continuous unitary representation of a second-countable locally compact type-I group admits a direct integral over its actual dual with measurable positive finite or countably infinite multiplicity; almost every fibre is the indicated irreducible amplification. Null-support fibres may be zero, and the zero representation uses zero measure.

Assume AC. For a separable strongly continuous representation of a second-countable locally compact type-I group, two dual-labelled decompositions as in the existence theorem have equivalent measures and equal multiplicities almost everywhere.

Assume AC. On a nonempty compact Riemann surface with a Hermitian holomorphic line bundle and compatible metric, the Dolbeault form domain equals H¹ with equivalent norms and smooth graph-norm density. An H¹ distributional solution Δ''u=f with f∈Hᵏ lies in Hᵏ⁺² and satisfies the stated estimate by the Hᵏ norm of f and the L² norm of u.

Assume AC. The resolvent B=(I+Δ'')⁻¹ is compact, positive and self-adjoint. On the orthogonal complement of the harmonic kernel, G=B(I−B)⁻¹ is compact, positive, self-adjoint and injective, has range dom(Δ'')∩H⊥, and satisfies both Green identities with bounded H² gain.

Assume AC. On a nonempty compact connected Riemann surface with the supplied bundle and metrics, smooth and L² degreewise Dolbeault spaces split orthogonally into harmonic and exact or adjoint-image summands; the Hilbert ranges are closed, the harmonic projections are bounded on every Hᵏ, and each smooth degree-one Dolbeault class has a unique harmonic representative.

Assume AC. The conjugate-linear bundle star identifies harmonic E-valued (0,1)-forms with H⁰(X,K⊗E*), commutes with the indicated smooth Dolbeault Laplacians, and the well-defined complex-bilinear pairing ∫u∧α is perfect, giving H⁰,¹(X,E)≅H⁰(X,K⊗E*)*.

Assume AC. For a holomorphic line bundle on a compact Riemann surface with supplied metrics, H⁰,⁰ equals the finite-dimensional holomorphic-section and harmonic space; H⁰,¹ is finite-dimensional with unique harmonic representatives. Both dimensions are independent of the supplied metrics.

Assume AC. Borel relations with nonempty sections between standard-Borel spaces admit Borel selectors on conull Borel subsets of a sigma-finite measured base. Bounded Borel sectionwise suprema have Borel versions outside Borel null sets, and countably many such constructions share one conull base.

Assume AC. A nondegenerate concrete C*-algebra is strongly dense in its bicommutant with unit-ball density. When the bicommutant is B(H), compatible finite self-adjoint prescriptions are realized exactly; the separate spectral-clipping clause preserves prescribed eigenvectors. Inequivalent pure GNS states have norm distance two, and pure states at distance less than two are internally unitarily equivalent.

Assume AC. For every second-countable locally compact non-type-I group, some separable strongly continuous representation has two equivalent irreducible direct integrals whose components are inequivalent for every cross pair; central factor decomposition remains canonical.

alerts.finding: Proof 2.1 says: 'The commutant of π_*(C*(G)) is scalar by [F1], so its strong closure is B(H) by the double-commutant theorem.' The cited owned theorem thm-double-commutant-theorem-for-concrete-von-neumann-algebras supplies finite-tuple density for a unital star algebra. The represented C*(G) image is only stipulated nondegenerate, and need not be unital. The short nonunital extension of this application is left implicit; the required extension is proved explicitly in lem-bounded-density-and-finite-vector-transitivity-for-c-star-representations, Proof 1.1 and 2.1.

seams_checked.note: Classification F7/Proof 8.1 faithfully uses separability and GCR⇒type I, without needing the reverse Glimm implication. Plancherel F3/F4/F10/F14 and Proof 4.1–10.1 retain the standard-Borel, conull-selection, effective nonzero-fibre and canonical multiplicity hypotheses. The exception is classification Proof 2.1's implicit extension of the cited unital bicommutant density argument to a nonunital nondegenerate image, recorded in alerts. The exact Glimm and Dixmier citation exceptions were checked against research/frontier-43-complex-representation-15-conditional-glimm-citation-authorization.json; this dispatch does not claim original-source reading.

The comparison theorem restricts the maximal operator to smooth sections and does not prematurely identify a Hilbert cokernel. Finiteness F7 retains compactness, supplied metrics and AC. The genus, nondegeneracy and Serre-duality uses retain the canonical twist K⊗E*, conjugate-linear star, unique smooth harmonic representatives and complex-bilinear pairing. The residue pairing's additional factor (2πi)⁻¹ is stated by its own supplier and is not attributed to the Hodge theorem.
